md: - **G7 members:** USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, **Canada** (EU attends); **Netherlands** and **New Zealand** are **not** members.
- **NATO-Russia Council (May 2002):** Russia **never joined** NATO (founded 1949); newest members **Finland (2023)** and **Sweden (2024)**.
- **Earlier G20 summits:** 2017 **Hamburg**, 2018 **Buenos Aires**, 2019 **Osaka** (Japan), 2020 **Riyadh** (virtual), 2022 **Bali** - theme "**Recover Together, Recover Stronger**".
- **GBA non-G20 supporters:** **Paraguay, Sri Lanka, Guyana, Seychelles, Finland**, Iceland, Kenya, Uganda, UAE; **Chile** is **not** among them.
- **International Year of Planet Earth (2008):** backed by **UNESCO + IUGS**; science themes included "**Transparent Earth**" and "Earth Inside".
- **BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection MoU (2017):** power-sector grid link among the **7 members**; secretariat **Dhaka**.
- **16th SAARC Summit:** **Thimphu**, **28-29 April 2010** (not 18-19 April); theme "**Towards a Green and Happy South Asia**".

- **NAM summits:** 14th **Havana** (2006), 15th **Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt** (July 2009), 16th **Tehran** (2012); NAM founded at **Belgrade (1961)**.
- **CICA:** proposed by Kazakhstan's **Nazarbayev (1992)**; first summit **Almaty, June 2002** adopted the **Almaty Act** - **Thailand** did not sign.

- **WEF Davos 2017:** theme "**Responsive and Responsible Leadership**"; attended by **Xi Jinping**.
- **77th Indian History Congress (2016):** **Thiruvananthapuram**, hosted by the **University of Kerala**.
- **International Ayurveda Congress 2017:** held in **London**.
- **New Delhi World Book Fair 2017:** theme "**Manushi**" (writings on and by women); organised by the **National Book Trust**.
- **ET Global Business Summit 2019:** **New Delhi**.
- **5th India-Arab Partnership Conference:** **Dubai**; organised with **FICCI** and the **League of Arab States**.
- **World Council of Religious Leaders:** met in **Bangkok (June 2002)**, after the UN Millennium World Peace Summit (2000).

after: Both the WMO and IAEA heads
md:
- **WHO:** **Tedros** became DG in **2017**, the **first African** head, succeeding **Margaret Chan**.
- **IMF:** **Christine Lagarde** was MD **2011-2019** (later **ECB** President); **Georgieva** from 2019.
- **World Telecommunication Development Conference:** held by the **ITU** every **four years**.
- **International Solar Alliance:** **Malta** became its **119th member**.
- **EU Constitution:** drafted by the European Convention under **Valery Giscard d'Estaing**; failed in **2005** referendums; replaced by the **Lisbon Treaty (2009)**.
- **Makli necropolis**, near **Thatta (Sindh, Pakistan)**: one of the world's largest; UNESCO World Heritage Site (**1981**).
- **OECD** (Paris, **38** members) publishes "**Promoting Strong and Inclusive Growth**".

- **India-South Africa MoU:** Cabinet-approved cooperation in the **disability sector** (assistive technology, expertise exchange).
- **Maitree Express (April 2008):** **Kolkata-Dhaka**, rail link restored after **43 years**; **Bandhan Express** (2017) = Kolkata-**Khulna**.
- **India-Vietnam:** Friendship Festival **2007** in **New Delhi**; **Strategic Partnership 2007**, **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership 2016**.
- **Republic Day chief guests:** **Barack Obama** (2015), **Francois Hollande** (2016).
- **Training academies:** **IMA Dehradun** (1932), **NDA Khadakwasla** (Pune), **OTA Chennai and Gaya**, **Air Force Academy Dundigal**, **Naval Academy Ezhimala**.

# Earlier world events
- **ObamaCare:** US **Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (2010)** on health insurance.
- **Aleppo** (Syria): major battleground of the **Syrian civil war**.
- **Venezuela** demonetised its **100-bolivar** note after India (December 2016), then backtracked.
- **Greece referendum (July 2015):** voters rejected **EU-IMF bailout** terms; the Tsipras government later accepted a new bailout.
- **Brexit vote (2016):** Cameron resigned; **Theresa May** (Conservative) became PM - **not** the opposition.
- **France (March 2024):** first country to make **abortion** a constitutional right.
- **PNG PM James Marape:** first **Pacific leader** to address **Australia's Parliament** (Feb 2024).
- **Trinidad and Tobago:** national emergency over an offshore **oil spill** (Feb 2024).
- **Rain Vortex** (about 40 m): world's tallest indoor waterfall, **Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore**.
- **"East Wind" (Jan 2017):** first **China-London** freight train, from **Yiwu**, under the Belt and Road.
- **UK general election, 6 May 2010** (not 5 May): hung parliament; **Cameron-led** Conservative-Lib Dem coalition.
- **US 9/11 Commission:** chaired by **Thomas Kean**; vice-chair Lee Hamilton; report July 2004.
- **Musharraf** survived two bomb attacks in **Rawalpindi** (14 and 25 December 2003).
- **East Timor (Timor-Leste):** former **Portuguese** colony; annexed by Indonesia 1976; independent **20 May 2002**.

# Earlier heads abroad
- **Brazil:** President **Dilma Rousseff** impeached by the Senate (**2016**); **Michel Temer** succeeded.
- **Guatemala:** **Bernardo Arevalo** President from **2024**; **Liberia:** **Joseph Boakai**.
- **Turkey:** **Abdullah Gul** President **2007-2014**; Erdogan then PM, President from 2014.
- **Cuba:** **Raul Castro** President from **February 2008**, succeeding Fidel; **Diaz-Canel** from 2018.
- **Germany:** ex-IMF chief **Horst Kohler** became President in **2004**.
- **Maldives:** **Maumoon Abdul Gayoom** ruled **1978-2008**; new term November 2003; defeated by **Mohamed Nasheed** (2008).
- **UK:** **Paul Boateng** - first black Cabinet minister (**2002**), Chief Secretary to the Treasury.
- **Louisiana:** **Kathleen Blanco** beat **Bobby Jindal** (2003), first woman Governor; Jindal won in 2007.
- **Academie Francaise** (1635, Richelieu): elected **Giscard d'Estaing** an "Immortal" (2003).

- **Gen. M.M. Naravane:** Vice Chief (Sept 2019), then **Army Chief from 31 Dec 2019**, succeeding **Bipin Rawat** (first **CDS**).
- **Anil Baijal:** **Lieutenant Governor of Delhi** (December 2016), replacing **Najeeb Jung**.
- **National Book Trust (1957):** historian **Bipan Chandra** became Chairman in **2004**.
- **Vande Bharat (Train 18):** semi-high-speed **EMU**; design speed **180 km/h**, operated up to **160 km/h** (not 250).
